To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a cytokine profile associated with bronchopopulmonary dysplastic disease or death in extremely low birth weight newborns.
cytokine levels are associated with the development of bronchopulmary dysplasia/dead in infants born with extremely low birth weight.

the development of bronchopulmary dysplasia or death in extremely low birth weight (less than 1000 g) infants is associated with higher concentrations in blood of the cytokines interleukin 6, 10, and 1β, interferon γ, and tumor necrosin factor β and lower concentrations of the cytokines regulated on activation, normalized T cell expressed, and secreted; interleukin 8; and 17.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cytokines in the development of bronchopulmonay dysplasia.
the development of predictive models of bronchopulmary dysplasia (BPD) and death among extremely low-birth weight infants.
the development of a new model to predict bronchopulmonary disease in extremely low birth weight neonates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data support the hypothesis that cytokines may be important in the etiology of bronchopulmary dysplasia, but the data are inconclusive regarding the clinical utility of the cytokine profile for prediction of bronchopulmory dysplasia.
the addition of cytokines to clinical variables improves prediction for the outcome of death or bronchopulmonary disease, but the magnitude of improvement is modest.
cytokines are not predictive of BPD, but the results of the study do provide insight into the pathobiology of BPD and suggest that cytokines are associated with BPD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytokine pattern associated with bronchopulymonary dysplasia is consistent with an impaired transition from the innate to the adaptive immune system.
we have identified a set of cytokine markers that may be useful in the future to predict the development of bronchopulmary dysplasia/deaths.
the cytokine pattern associated with bronchopu- monary dysplasia or death suggests that the transition from innate to adaptive immunity is impaired in extremely low birth weight neonates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although cytokine measurements may improve the predictive ability of multivariate logistic regression, the improvement is modest.
the cytokine profile of infants who go on to develop BPD is not a unique profile.

cytokines may have a role to play in predicting the development of bronchopulmary dysplasia in extremely preterm infants, and that this role is likely to be more complex than a single cytokine or a few cytokines.
